articles.summary: Government employee fraud has led to a wire fraud guilty plea from Nehemie Almonor, a 41-year-old human resources specialist from King George, Virginia,
articles.body: Government employee fraud has led to a wire fraud guilty plea from Nehemie Almonor, a 41-year-old human resources specialist from King George, Virginia, in the Eastern District of Virginia. Court documents state that between May 2022 and at least April 2025, she electronically submitted timecards certifying full-time telework for several employers during overlapping hours. They included a private company and multiple federal government organisations. Prosecutors put the combined amount defrauded from her employers at no less than $291,905. She entered the plea on 1 April 2026, following an investigation by the Transportation Security Administration’s Office of Law Enforcement and Investigations.Timecards that claimed 120 hours or more of full-time work within a single 40-hour periodThe United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia said in a press release that Almonor commonly submitted timecards for full-time work at three positions simultaneously. Added together, they attested to 120 hours or more of work in single 40-hour periods. Beyond the private company, the employers named were the Transportation Security Administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, the Food and Drug Administration and the Air Force Reserves.Three work laptops kept open side by side, and complaints that she could not be reachedProsecutors say Almonor commonly kept at least three work laptops open next to each other, so that each employer would believe she was online and working full-time only for them. The Transportation Security Administration received multiple complaints that she was often unreachable during the very hours she had certified on her timecards, at a time when she held at least three full-time positions.Telling other agencies she was unemployed, and claiming full-time work while on military ordersWhile in various full-time telework positions, Almonor applied to other government agencies and described herself as unemployed, and so available to start immediately. She also claimed full-time work during a period of military orders with the United States Air Force, at the same time as she claimed full-time work for three other entities.Almonor was scheduled to be sentenced on 22 July and faces up to 20 years in prison, the same office said. A federal district court judge will decide any sentence after considering the United States Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.Special Assistant United States Attorney Jake Drucker is prosecuting the case, filed under case number 1:26-cr-45. Related court documents can be found on the website of the district court for the Eastern District of Virginia, or through the federal courts’ records system, Public Access to Court Electronic Records, by searching that number.You use AI every day. articles.title: Delhi to Agra in 59 minutes, Lucknow in 2 hours and Varanasi in 3.5 hours: PM Modi approves bullet train corridor that could bring North India's top destinations closer
articles.summary: In a recent major travel update, India Prime Minister Narendra Modi has approved the Northern Corridor of India's bullet train network.
articles.body: In a recent major travel update, India Prime Minister Narendra Modi has approved the Northern Corridor of India's bullet train network. When completed, the journey from Delhi to Agra could only take just 59 minutes, while reaching Lucknow may take a little over two hours. The news was announced by Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on October 31, 2026.As per update, the minister announced the development in Varanasi ahead of flagging off the new Vande Bharat Sleeper Express between Varanasi and New Delhi, as reported by the Press Trust of India (PTI) and Akashvani.Vaishnaw said, "The prime minister has approved the north corridor of the bullet train, which will change the lives of many. The vision for the bullet train shared by the prime minister will greatly benefit the youth, the middle-income group, and artisans in small-scale industries. People will remember Prime Minister Modi for the next 100 years for this initiative."More about the proposed corridorThe proposed corridor will start in Delhi and connect the following cities:AgraKanpurLucknowAyodhyaVaranasiPrayagrajPatnaSiliguri before extending to Guwahati in AssamNot only this, the network is expected to reduce travel times significantly between important cities, making intercity journeys faster for tourists, business travellers and students.Delhi to Agra in 59 minutes?Vaishnaw also said that passengers would be able to travel between Delhi and Agra in just 59 minutes when completed.The Delhi-Agra connection could be important from a tourism point of view. Agra, home to the Taj Mahal, attracts domestic and international visitors throughout the year. A journey of less than an hour could make it easier for travellers to plan day trips from Delhi.Other proposed journey times include:Delhi to Agra: 59 minutesDelhi to Kanpur: 1 hour 45 minutesDelhi to Lucknow: 2 hours 12 minutesLucknow to Varanasi: 1 hour 21 minutesVaranasi to Delhi: 3 hours 35 minutesThese are still indicative journey times shared by the Railway Minister and not the final timings. The government has not yet announced a detailed station-wise timetable for the proposed corridor.Which cities will the Northern Bullet Train Corridor connectThe proposed route is expected to cover a large geographical stretch.As per update, the first stretch will connect Delhi with Agra and Kanpur, followed by Lucknow and Ayodhya. The network will then extend towards Varanasi and Prayagraj before connecting with Patna and Siliguri. Its proposed extension to Guwahati will provide high-speed rail connectivity towards the Northeast.For tourists, this could mean easier access to several popular destinations including Ayodhya and Varanasi which are two of India's major religious tourism hubs.Prayagraj is known for the Triveni Sangam and the Kumbh Mela. Patna serves as an important gateway to Bihar's historical and Buddhist tourism destinations, while Siliguri is a major transit point for travellers heading to Darjeeling, Sikkim and other parts of the eastern Himalayas.Bullet train project to be built under Make in India initiative"The construction is progressing rapidly. It will be fully 'Make in India', built by the youth and welders of India," the minister said speaking about the project's construction.He also said the proposed high-speed rail network would benefit young people, middle-income groups and artisans working in small-scale industries. Addressing concerns about affordability, he indicated that bullet train fares would be economical and lower than airfares.What is the latest official update on India's bullet train network?The Northern Corridor announcement comes amid the government's broader push to expand high-speed rail connectivity across the country.In a February 3, 2026, Press Information Bureau (PIB) release on the Union Budget 2026-27, the Ministry of Railways outlined several proposed high-speed rail connections, including Delhi-Varanasi and Varanasi-Siliguri. The official release projected a journey time of around 3 hours 50 minutes between Delhi and Varanasi and approximately 2 hours 55 minutes between Varanasi and Siliguri.The latest announcement by Vaishnaw provides further details about the proposed Northern Corridor and its expected journey times. However, important project details, including the final alignment, station locations, construction cost, implementation schedule and expected opening date, are yet to be officially announced.You use AI every day. articles.title: Meerut's infamous 'blue drum murder house' to be cleaned, painted and 'purified' after Diwali
articles.summary: MEERUT: Nearly 19 months after a merchant navy officer was murdered inside a rented house in Meerut, the property is set for a ritual intended to cleanse
articles.body: MEERUT: Nearly 19 months after a merchant navy officer was murdered inside a rented house in Meerut, the property is set for a ritual intended to cleanse it of the memories of the crime.The house owner, Ompal Singh, said a "shuddhikaran" (purification ritual) and a "havan" would be held after Diwali in the part of the house where Saurabh Rajput was killed.The premises will also be thoroughly cleaned and painted before they are put to use again.The house in Indira Nagar, in Meerut's Brahmpuri area, had remained sealed since Saurabh's murder on March 3, 2025. His wife Muskan and her lover Sahil murdered him, dismembered his body and concealed the remains in a blue drum filled with cement.Both were convicted in the case and sentenced to death.The property was reopened last Wednesday in the presence of police personnel. After breaking the locks, officers inventoried the belongings left inside and handed them over to Saurabh's brother, Rahul alias Bablu.For the family, returning to the house was an emotional ordeal. Saurabh's mother, Renu Devi, and his brother broke down in tears when they entered the room where he had been killed.Saurabh, who worked in the merchant navy, was killed inside the house he shared with Muskan as a tenant.Police arrested Muskan and Sahil on March 18, 2025.The Allahabad high court on Tuesday fixed November 30 for hearing an appeal filed by Muskan and Sahil challenging the death sentence awarded to them by a Meerut court.A bench of Justices Salil Kumar Rai and Padam Narain Mishra passed the order on the appeal filed by the two convicts.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Meerut | Silver Rate in Meerut | Bank Holidays in Meerut | Public Holidays in Meerut | Meerut AQI | Weather in Meerut | Petrol Price in Meerut | Diesel Price in Meerut | CNG Price in Meerut | LPG Price in MeerutStay updated with the latest Meerut news. articles.title: Fat-dissolving claims land FatX Solution in regulatory trouble; CDSCO cancels registration
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Promising to dissolve fat cells may sound like an attractive pitch for a slimming product, but it has landed FatX Solution in trouble with the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Promising to dissolve fat cells may sound like an attractive pitch for a slimming product, but it has landed FatX Solution in trouble with the country's drug regulator. The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has cancelled the product's registration after finding that it was being promoted with claims that are not permitted for cosmetics.In an order dated October 28, CDSCO said Delhi-based importer Tekno Midas Aesthetics was marketing FatX Solution on its website as a product that could dissolve fat cells and reduce their size. The regulator said these were drug-related claims and did not fit the definition of a cosmetic under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.The action followed a scrutiny of the company's application and website, during which CDSCO found differences between the claims being made online and those mentioned on the approved product label.Under the Cosmetics Rules, 2020, cosmetic products cannot make false or misleading claims. The rules define cosmetics as products meant for cleansing, beautifying, promoting attractiveness or altering appearance. Claims to dissolve fat cells go beyond this definition, the regulator said.CDSCO had issued a show-cause notice to the company on August 10, citing violations of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act and the Cosmetics Rules. The company submitted its response on September 1, but the regulator found it inconclusive and unsatisfactory. The firm also requested that its registration certificate be voluntarily surrendered.Rajan Bhatnagar of Tekno Midas Aesthetics told TOI that the product had been registered as a cosmetic more than four years ago. "At that time, the licence was granted because the product was registered as a cosmetic. The authorities have now changed their interpretation of the category under which the product falls. Earlier, it was considered a cosmetic, but now they say it falls under another category," he said.He said the company had decided not to contest the matter after receiving the notice. "We did not want to get into any dispute or challenge the notification. We voluntarily requested the surrender of the licence, and the authorities cancelled it," he said.The Central Licensing Authority subsequently cancelled the registration certificate, RC/COS-003300, which was issued in July 2022 and was valid until July 14, 2027. The cancellation took effect from October 28.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How do you score 171 out of 170 in a Harvard Exam
articles.summary: In a recent conversation with The Times of India, Impact Catalyst Aruna Lohia Goenka unveiled YASHA, her five-pillar framework for Viksit Bharat 2047:
articles.body: In a recent conversation with The Times of India, Impact Catalyst Aruna Lohia Goenka unveiled YASHA, her five-pillar framework for Viksit Bharat 2047: Yuva, Anna, Shiksha, Hunar and Abundance, shaped by nearly 30 years of engagement in national development.The knowledge series, under the overarching theme of Viksit Bharat 2047, now takes that conversation further. Across five interviews, Sanjiv Kaura, CEO-CSR, The Times of India, explores the experiences, convictions and ideas behind each pillar of the YASHA framework.We begin with S for Shiksha.Sanjiv Kaura: As we approach a world in which machines may become more intelligent than human beings, what is the greatest danger facing our children?Aruna Goenka: The danger is not that machines will become more intelligent. It is that humans may stop thinking and become like robots: programmed to respond, but forgetting how to feel, empathise and connect.Sanjiv Kaura: Can you share an example of an educational intervention that reflects this philosophy?Aruna Goenka: In the tribal district of Bastar, Chhattisgarh, we taught children how to think, rather than what to think. That was in the 1990s. The greatest moment is not when a child says, "I know the answer." It is when the child asks, "But why?" Today, 30 years later, I feel blessed to be associated with the AM/NS India Times Critical Thinking Championship, which reaches 1 million children each year across 28 states and 8 Union Territories in 14 languages. The scale has changed enormously, but the underlying conviction remains the same.Sanjiv Kaura: If AI can become a personal tutor to every child, will we still need teachers?Aruna Goenka: More than ever! AI may explain Einstein’s and Newton's laws, but can it recognise the child who has stopped believing in herself? A machine can deliver a lesson, but a great teacher can change a life. AI should be our children's co-pilot, not their autopilot.Sanjiv Kaura: Are we sometimes confusing marks with intelligence?Aruna Goenka: (Laughs) We give children marks for answering questions correctly. Perhaps we should reward them much more for asking questions nobody else thought of! And who says 100% is the ceiling? Let me tell you a fascinating story. In December 2018, an IIT alum and IAS officer, Ankur Garg, studying at Harvard Kennedy School, scored 171 marks out of 170 in a macroeconomics examination conducted by the world-renowned economist Professor Jeffrey Frankel. Yes, you heard that correctly. 171 out of 170! Now, isn't that wonderful?For me, that is a beautiful metaphor for education and life. Never allow someone else's definition of the maximum to become the limit of your potential. And why restrict this philosophy to examinations? Whether it is knowledge, kindness, compassion or service, give more than is expected of you. After all, a100% cent may be the examiner's limit. It need not be the limit of human potential.Sanjiv Kaura: Socrates famously argued that the unexamined life is not worth living. Are we losing sight of that larger purpose of education?Aruna Goenka: Absolutely, Socrates was reminding us that a meaningful life must be examined, not merely lived. For him, the pursuit of wisdom was inseparable from virtue. Compassion, honesty, courage, self-discipline and consciousness are not optional extras in education. They are at its very heart.And education is not confined to degrees. Think of the extraordinary wisdom ancient Bharat produced: the Upanishads, Tirukkural, Yoga Sutras, Charaka Samhita, and Panchatantra. Consider Gautam Buddha's teachings on compassion and mindfulness; Lord Mahavira's Anekantavada, which reminds us that truth has many facets and no single viewpoint captures its entirety; Kabir's fearless questioning of dogma; Guru Nanak's message of equality and service; Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, with its timeless reflections on duty and devotion, and Kahlil Gibran's timeless wisdom on love, self-discovery and nurturing of independent minds across centuries and civilisations, these extraordinary minds explored not merely how much we can know, but how wisely we can live. Their insights continue to inspire humanity even today. I believe we must cultivate the awareness to discover the possibilities present in the Universe; otherwise, surrounded by information and technology, we risk becoming intellectual zombies!Sanjiv Kaura: You come from a family blessed with Lakshmi (prosperity), yet your affection for Saraswati (knowledge) seems just as profound!Aruna Goenka: (With a twinkle in her eyes) I come from a family of geniuses and wizards! My elder brother has one of the world's largest collections of handwritten books/manuscripts. Imagine the centuries of knowledge, imagination and wisdom preserved in those pages. I have never seen Lakshmi and Saraswati as rivals but as two complementary forces within us. Lakshmi symbolises the subconscious mind, where dreams are born, while Saraswati represents the conscious mind, which gives direction to the dreams. And remember, Lakshmi does not stay where Saraswati is neglected. Wealth without wisdom never creates lasting abundance.Sanjiv Kaura: We sometimes celebrate the silver spoon. But listening to you, I wonder whether a Silva Mind is the greater inheritance.Aruna Goenka: (Laughs) Interestingly, I have seen the Silva Mind technique being used by my elder brother for decades – I saw him reading a book about it when he was just fourteen! The power of visualisation fascinated me. I believe it helped him envision extraordinary possibilities and turn them into reality, including the remarkable library he eventually built. But I like your comparison. A silver spoon may feed the body, but a silver mind feeds curiosity. And I must say, there is something wonderful about knowledge. It is perhaps the only inheritance that becomes richer the more you give it away.Sanjiv Kaura: Which are some of your favourite books?Aruna Goenka: Oh, Sanjiv, that's like asking a mother to choose her favourite child! (Laughs) But a few have stayed with me. Autobiography of a Yogi opens our minds to spirituality, consciousness and life's infinite possibilities. Then there is Thoreau's Walden, which reminds us that a rich life need not be a complicated one. And I love Ralph Waldo Emerson's essay Self-Reliance, with its powerful message about trusting one's own judgment rather than blindly following the crowd. Another favourite is Critical Thinking by Richard Paul. And here's a lovely coincidence! Only recently, I discovered that my younger brother has been reading it since the early 1990s! Imagine - all these years, we have been travelling along similar intellectual paths without even realising it.Sanjiv Kaura: Aruna ji, your closing thoughts?Aruna Goenka: Literacy teaches us to read, education teaches us to understand, and wisdom teaches us to question. Literacy opens the book. Education opens the mind. Wisdom opens the heart. And above all, dream big! But why confine your dreams to the night? Dream during the day, with your eyes wide open, and work to turn those dreams into reality. Imagine 1.4 billion people, each with a dream for Bharat, and each determined to make it happen! When 1.4 billion dreams become 1.4 billion actions, Viksit Bharat 2047 will not be just a vision. It will be our reality!Disclaimer: This article has been produced on behalf of Aruna Goenka for Times Foundation as part of the Knowledge Sharing Series and published by Times Internet's Spotlight team.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
